strings.name: David Patterson
strings.summary: Patterson studied at UCLA and joined Berkeley in 1976. With teams he advanced reduced instruction set computing and RAID disk arrays; his architecture textbooks with John Hennessy influenced processor design, storage reliability and engineering education. They shared the 2017 Turing Award. After retirement he continued computing research and work to bring research into practice.
strings.coverageNote: Selected milestones verifiable through 13 November 2026; not a live news archive.
strings.influence.rationale: He advanced research on RISC processors and storage systems, and contributed to computer architecture education and the development of the open hardware ecosystem.

strings.highlights.h1.title: RISC research
strings.highlights.h1.text: He led Berkeley RISC research, exploring with his team the performance potential of simpler instruction designs.
strings.highlights.h2.title: RAID and textbooks
strings.highlights.h2.text: He advanced disk-array research with collaborators and co-authored widely used architecture textbooks with Hennessy.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Invited to discuss AI and public good
strings.timeline.t1.text: Georgia State announced his King-Cole lecture; this source establishes the invitation, not that the lecture had taken place.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Turing Award announced
strings.timeline.t2.text: ACM announced that he and John Hennessy shared the 2017 Turing Award for contributions to computer architecture.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Retires from Berkeley
strings.timeline.t3.text: After nearly four decades on Berkeley’s faculty, he became professor emeritus and continued computing research in industry.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Becomes ACM president
strings.timeline.t4.text: He began his 2004–2006 ACM presidency, contributing to the organization of the computing profession.
strings.timeline.t5.title: RAID paper
strings.timeline.t5.text: With Garth Gibson and Randy Katz, he published a RAID paper examining disk arrays as a means to improve storage systems.
strings.timeline.t6.title: RISC I design
strings.timeline.t6.text: With Carlo Séquin, he published RISC I research combining reduced instruction sets with VLSI design.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Joins Berkeley
strings.timeline.t7.text: After completing his UCLA PhD, he joined UC Berkeley to teach and conduct architecture research.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Earns mathematics degree
strings.timeline.t8.text: He earned a UCLA mathematics bachelor’s degree before pursuing graduate study in computer science.
